review_title: Paragraph-by-paragraph completeness and accuracy review of the Uzi Meshulam prison letter translation
review_standard: Scholastic formal equivalence: every clause, negation, connective, pronoun, tense, technical term, quotation, citation, acronym, gematria, parenthesis, repetition, and polemical assertion was checked. Source irregularities were not silently corrected. Bracketed citation identifications, acronym expansions, and technical glosses documented in the translation notes were treated as transparent editorial apparatus rather than omissions or covert normalization.

verdict_scale.pass: Complete and accurate under the stated register; no correction required.
verdict_scale.minor_revision: Complete overall, but a localized wording change is required for exact semantic or syntactic fidelity.
verdict_scale.major_revision: Material omission, addition, mistranslation, doctrinal smoothing, or paragraph-level failure requiring substantial replacement.

issues.hebrew: וידוע שסוד משיח מקנא מאוד להשי״ת
issues.draft: And it is known that the mystery of Messiah is exceedingly zealous for the Blessed Name
issues.analysis: The draft makes “the mystery of Messiah” the agent that is zealous. In the elliptical Hebrew, סוד introduces the mystical proposition or aspect, while משיח is the personal agent who is zealous. The present English is grammatically possible only by personifying “mystery,” and thus slightly obscures the polemical assertion about Messiah himself. All wordplay, quotations, citations, technical terminology, and the אפינו/ניאוף anagram elsewhere in the paragraph are complete and accurate.

paragraphs.proposed_replacement_wording: And it is known that, in the mystery of Messiah, Messiah is exceedingly zealous for the Blessed Name and wages war to eradicate the blemish of fornication from the world, as stated: “The breath of our nostrils, the Messiah of the Lord” [Lamentations 4:20]—opposed to, and in order to break and eradicate, the letters of “fornication” [ni’uf; ניאוף, an anagram of אפינו, “our nostrils”].

issues.hebrew: ויספרו ויתפשטו עליו כל מיני מניעות וקטרוגים
issues.draft: and they will relate and disseminate concerning him every kind of hindrance and accusation
issues.analysis: The Hebrew coordinates a passive/impersonal reporting verb with an intransitive spreading verb: hindrances and accusations will be told and will spread over him. The draft instead gives an unspecified plural human subject (“they”) both transitive verbs and makes hindrances themselves things that people “disseminate.” No content is omitted, but the agency and the force of ויתפשטו עליו shift.

paragraphs.proposed_replacement_wording: “And they will speak about him such falsehoods and lies as could not be believed if related,” and every kind of hindrance and accusation will be related concerning him and will spread over him, and he will be in great hiddenness and concealment from the world—this is the mystery of the soul of our righteous Messiah, who will be revealed speedily in our days.

issues.analysis: כליון נפש here denotes consuming yearning or intense longing, not the soul literally expiring. The calque “with expiring soul” risks asserting death or physical expiration and does not convey the idiom’s actual devotional force. The anomalous self-designation “Uzi Azulai,” the parentage, all prayer clauses, negations, acronyms, and the Aramaic conclusion are otherwise preserved without normalization.

paragraphs.proposed_replacement_wording: Master of the Universe, I, Your servant Uzi Azulai, son of Rabbi David and Tziona, wait with consuming longing for the revelation of the illumination of our righteous Messiah. Please help me. You are my Father, my God, and the Rock of my salvation: [help me] to rectify my ways thoroughly, so that, Heaven forbid, I shall not be among those who delay the coming of the Redeemer; and may we merit, speedily in our days, amen, that our righteous Messiah come at our head, and that we ascend to Jerusalem with everlasting gladness, to raise His Shekhinah from the dust.

issues.hebrew: גודל המניעות והיסורין והכסויים שצריכין לעבור על כל מי שרוצה להתקרב אל האמת
issues.draft: the magnitude of the hindrances, sufferings, and coverings through which everyone who wishes to draw near to the truth must pass
issues.analysis: The Hebrew says that the hindrances, sufferings, and coverings must pass over/befall each person; the draft reverses the syntactic trajectory and has each person pass through them. The experiential meaning is close, but strict formal equivalence requires retaining the source’s “pass over/befall” construction.

paragraphs.proposed_replacement_wording: For it is impossible to suckle from, and be sanctified by, the true righteous one except through literal self-sacrifice, as we see perceptibly the magnitude of the hindrances, sufferings, and coverings that must pass over everyone who wishes to draw near to the truth; he must endure sufferings to the point of the crushing of the soul.

no_truncation_verdict.statement: All 37 nonempty Hebrew paragraphs correspond in order to exactly 37 nonempty English paragraphs. No Hebrew paragraph, terminal clause, quotation continuation, parenthesis, repeated phrase, acronym, gematria, signature element, or final Na Naḥ formula is omitted or truncated. The blank physical separator before the final formula is not a source paragraph and is consistently excluded from both nonempty-paragraph counts.
cross_paragraph_checks: The Isaiah 12 quotation that opens in paragraph 8 continues and closes in paragraph 9 in the English as in the Hebrew.
The syntactic continuation from paragraph 9 into paragraph 10 is retained.
The comma-led continuation from paragraph 22 into paragraph 23 is retained.

The long and textually irregular paragraph 29 is present in full, including both quotations, the parenthetical “not to become acquainted!”, the Likkutei Halakhot reference, the parrot explanation, the unresolved מד״ע acronym, the Ari citation, and the Arikh Anpin claim.
The signature in paragraph 36 and the standalone Na Naḥ Naḥma Naḥman me-Uman formula in paragraph 37 are both present.
